title: Load Balancer API
description: Load Balancers are highly available and fully managed [Instances](https://www.scaleway.com/en/docs/instances/concepts/#instance) that facilitate the distribution of incoming traffic across multiple servers. Load Balancers allow you to scale your applications while ensuring their continuous availability, even in the event of heavy traffic. They are commonly used to improve the performance and reliability of websites, applications, databases and other services.

glossary.action: Action to take when incoming traffic matches an ACL filter.
glossary.assign_flexible_ip: Defines whether to automatically assign a flexible public IP to the Load Balancer. Default value is `true` (assign).
glossary.assign_flexible_ipv6: Defines whether to automatically assign a flexible public IPv6 to the Load Balancer. Default value is `false` (do not assign).
glossary.backend: Backend object the frontend is attached to.
glossary.backend_count: Number of backends the Load Balancer has.
glossary.backends: List of backend objects of a given Load Balancer.
glossary.bandwidth: Maximum bandwidth for a given Load Balancer type.
glossary.certificate: Certificate, deprecated in favor of certificate_ids array.
glossary.certificate_chain: Full PEM-formatted certificate, consisting of the entire certificate chain including public key, private key, and (optionally) Certificate Authorities.
glossary.certificate_ids: List of SSL/TLS certificate IDs to bind to the frontend.
glossary.check_delay: Time to wait between two consecutive health checks. (in milliseconds)
glossary.check_max_retries: Number of consecutive unsuccessful health checks after which the server will be considered dead.
glossary.check_send_proxy: Defines whether proxy protocol should be activated for the health check.
glossary.check_timeout: Maximum time a backend server has to reply to the health check. (in milliseconds)
glossary.connection_rate_limit: Rate limit for new connections established on this frontend. Use 0 value to disable, else value is connections per second.
glossary.custom_certificate: Object to define an existing custom certificate to be imported.
glossary.email: Email address to send alerts to.
glossary.enable_access_logs: Defines whether to enable access logs on the frontend.
glossary.enable_http3: Defines whether to enable HTTP/3 protocol on the frontend.
glossary.failover_host: Scaleway Object Storage bucket website to be served as failover if all backend servers are down, e.g. failover-website.s3-website.fr-par.scw.cloud.
glossary.forward_port: Port used by the backend when forwarding traffic to backend servers.
glossary.forward_port_algorithm: Load balancing algorithm to use when determining which backend server to forward new traffic to.
glossary.forward_protocol: Protocol used by the backend when forwarding traffic to backend servers.
glossary.frontend: ACL is attached to this frontend object.
glossary.frontend_count: Number of frontends the Load Balancer has.
glossary.frontends: List of frontend objects of a given Load Balancer.
glossary.health_check: Object defining the health check to be carried out by the backend when checking the status and health of backend servers.
glossary.host:
Host value to use when connecting to backend servers.
When connecting to backend servers, use this value as the HTTP Host header or TLS SNI. This allows routing to specific services on the backend server that are configured to respond to particular hostnames.
glossary.http_config: Object to configure an HTTP health check.
glossary.http_filter: Type of HTTP filter to match. Extracts the request's URL path, which starts at the first slash and ends before the question mark (without the host part). Defines where to filter for the http_filter_value. Only supported for HTTP backends.
glossary.http_filter_option: Name of the HTTP header to filter on if `http_header_match` was selected in `http_filter`.
glossary.http_filter_value: List of values to filter for.
glossary.https_config: Object to configure an HTTPS health check.
glossary.ignore_ssl_server_verify: Defines whether the server certificate verification should be ignored.
glossary.index: Priority of this ACL (ACLs are applied in ascending order, 0 is the first ACL executed).
glossary.instance_id: ID of your Load Balancer's underlying Instance.
glossary.invert: Defines whether to invert the match condition. If set to `true`, the ACL carries out its action when the condition DOES NOT match.
glossary.ip_ids: List of IP IDs to attach to the Load Balancer.
glossary.ip_subnet: List of IPs or CIDR v4/v6 addresses to filter for from the client side.
glossary.ipam_ids: IPAM IDs of the booked IP addresses. (UUID format)
glossary.ips_edge_services: Defines whether Edge Services IPs should be matched. If set to `true`, restricts all connections except for Edge Services.
glossary.is_ipv6: If true, creates a Flexible IP with an ipv6 address.
glossary.lb_ids: Filter by lb_ids, only Load Balancers with these IDs will be returned.
glossary.lb_types: List of Load Balancer commercial offer type objects.
glossary.ldap_config: Object to configure an LDAP health check. The response is analyzed to find the LDAPv3 response message.
glossary.letsencrypt: Object to define a new Let's Encrypt certificate to be generated.
glossary.match_subdomains: If true, all subdomains will match.
glossary.max_connections: Maximum number of connections allowed per backend server.
glossary.max_retries: Number of retries when a backend server connection failed.
glossary.method:
HTTP method used for the health check.
The HTTP method used when performing a health check on backend servers.
glossary.multicloud: Ability to handle backend servers outside Scaleway for a given Load Balancer type.
glossary.mysql_config: Object to configure a MySQL health check. The check requires MySQL >=3.22 or <9.0. For older or newer versions, use a TCP health check.
glossary.on_marked_down_action: Action to take when a backend server is marked as down.
glossary.path_begin:
Path begin value to match.
Value to match in the URL beginning path from an incoming request.
glossary.pgsql_config: Object to configure a PostgreSQL health check.
glossary.pool: List of IP addresses of backend servers attached to this backend.
glossary.port: Port to use for the backend server health check.
glossary.private_network: List of Private Network objects attached to the Load Balancer.
glossary.private_network_count: Number of Private Networks attached to the Load Balancer.
glossary.proxy_protocol: Protocol to use between the Load Balancer and backend servers. Allows the backend servers to be informed of the client's real IP address. The PROXY protocol must be supported by the backend servers' software.
glossary.redirect: Redirection parameters when using an ACL with a `redirect` action.
glossary.redis_config: Object to configure a Redis health check. The response is analyzed to find the +PONG response message.
glossary.redispatch_attempt_count: Whether to use another backend server on each attempt.
glossary.release_ip: Defines whether the Load Balancer's flexible IP should be deleted. Set to true to release the flexible IP, or false to keep it available in your account for future Load Balancers.
glossary.reverse: Reverse DNS (domain name) of the IP address.
glossary.route_count: Number of routes configured on the Load Balancer.
glossary.send_proxy_v2: Deprecated in favor of proxy_protocol field.
glossary.server_state_changed_at: Time since last operational change. (RFC 3339 format)
glossary.ssl_bridging: Defines whether to enable SSL bridging between the Load Balancer and backend servers.
glossary.ssl_compatibility_level: Determines the minimal SSL version which needs to be supported on client side.
glossary.static_config: Object containing an array of a local IP address for the Load Balancer on this Private Network.
glossary.status_details: Additional information about the certificate status (useful in case of certificate generation failure, for example).
glossary.sticky_sessions: Defines whether sticky sessions (binding a particular session to a particular backend server) are activated and the method to use if so. None disables sticky sessions. Cookie-based uses an HTTP cookie to stick a session to a backend server. Table-based uses the source (client) IP address to stick a session to a backend server.
glossary.sticky_sessions_cookie_name: Cookie name for cookie-based sticky sessions.
glossary.stock_status: Current stock status for a given Load Balancer type.
glossary.target: Redirect target. For a location redirect, you can use a URL e.g. `https://scaleway.com`. Using a scheme name (e.g. `https`, `http`, `ftp`, `git`) will replace the request's original scheme. This can be useful to implement HTTP to HTTPS redirects. Valid placeholders that can be used in a `location` redirect to preserve parts of the original request in the redirection URL are \{\{host\}\}, \{\{query\}\}, \{\{path\}\} and \{\{scheme\}\}.
glossary.tcp_config: Object to configure a basic TCP health check.
glossary.timeout_client: Maximum allowed inactivity time on the client side. (in milliseconds)
glossary.timeout_connect: Maximum allowed time for establishing a connection to a backend server. (in milliseconds)
glossary.timeout_queue: Maximum time for a request to be left pending in queue when `max_connections` is reached. (in seconds)
glossary.timeout_server: Maximum allowed time for a backend server to process a request. (in milliseconds)
glossary.timeout_tunnel: Maximum allowed tunnel inactivity time after Websocket is established (takes precedence over client and server timeout). (in milliseconds)
glossary.transient_check_delay: Time to wait between two consecutive health checks when a backend server is in a transient state (going UP or DOWN). (in seconds)
